reference_roles.first: Current directional walk frame: identity/rendering target

WalkLeft: Edit the referenced pet into a production animation sprite atlas for a Windows desktop pet. The first image is the identity and rendering target: preserve exactly the same photographic fluffy white bichon frise, oversized round fluffy head, long hanging ear hair, short curly muzzle, small black eyes and nose, cheerful gently open mouth, red patterned collar with one gold bell, compact body and curled fluffy tail. The second reference reinforces bichon anatomy. Produce exactly TWELVE chronological phases of a relaxed natural four-legged WALK, not a run, in a perfectly regular grid of FOUR columns by THREE rows, row-major chronological order. Entire atlas aspect ratio 4:3, ideally 1536x1152; each cell square and equal. Every cell contains exactly one complete dog with generous transparent margins, no paws/ears/tail crossing cell boundaries. Fixed camera, same body dimensions and coat, identical head angle and size, same torso position and baseline inside every cell. Camera is side three-quarter view. All dogs face LEFT with the head pointing LEFT. Very important gait: all four legs flex and articulate at shoulder, elbow, hip and hock naturally; paws briefly lift and curl on swing and open softly on contact, rear legs do NOT remain straight or fixed like wooden sticks. A slow four-beat walk with alternating support, two or three paws touching a consistent ground line in every phase, feet traveling smoothly relative to the torso, no simultaneous airborne four-paw running pose. Complete exactly one smooth gait cycle: phase 0 contact, 1 weight transfer, 2 toe-off, 3 low foot recovery, 4 flexed swing, 5 forward reach, 6 opposite contact, 7 weight transfer, 8 toe-off, 9 low recovery, 10 flexed swing, 11 forward reach that flows naturally back into phase 0. Near and far legs staggered consistently. Subtle tail sway and almost no head bob; avoid head shaking or changing expressions. Natural paw contact and continuous joint articulation matter more than large exaggerated strides. Preserve original fur color and photographic detail, no cartoon redesign. Genuine transparent RGBA background across the entire atlas with no floor, drop shadow, background plate, grid lines, labels, text, numbers, borders or watermark. The pixels between cells must be completely transparent. Do not duplicate the same static pose for multiple frames. Do not mirror a left atlas to make a right atlas; render correct directional anatomy for this request.
